newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Fresh foreign capital pushes Hungary BUX to high.
newsitem.headline: Fresh foreign capital pushes Hungary BUX to high.

text.p: The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange soared to uncharted territory on Wednesday on the back of what investors saw as extremely encouraging macro news, traders and analysts said.

"The risk factors for earnings are lower in the sense that the pickup in the economy means more growth for Hungarian companies," said James Oates, director for central and eastern Europe at UBS in London. "That's pretty much unique in the region."
The BUX index surged to a new high of 6,793.20 points. At 1028 GMT it stood at 6,756.49 points, up 159.21 points or 2.41 percent from Tuesday's second successive closing high of 6,597.28 points.
Market participants agreed the market was bolstered by fresh capital from foreign investors who reacted positively to a batch of macro news on Tuesday.
"There is a continuous influx of fresh money, probably due to the rating," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.

On Tuesday, Hungary was upgraded to BBB from BBB- by IBCA, the monthly devalutor was cut to one percent from 1.1 percent from August 15 and the central bank cut its base rate to 21 percent from 21.50 percent from July 1.
"Mainly foreign investors are buying stocks in heavy volumes," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities, adding most of the fresh interest was likely to have come from overseas.
Some heavyweights led the market's surge, including chemicals TVK, oil company MOL and OTP Bank, all surging to new record highs.
Oates said, however, that the small size of the Hungarian market meant that a relatively small number of foreign investors could heavily influence it.
"A little bit of money goes a long way in Hungary because the market is very small," UBS's Oates added.
